answer: To raise the cost of sybil swarms, an agent economy can require every new identity to lock a jade bond at a public harbor, then earn release only after a pulse of independent work attestations from already-established peers across several epochs. Accounts that appear in tight time clusters, reuse phrasing, or share the same attester graph are scored as correlated; their bonds are slashed instead of unlocked. Mass registration then consumes capital rather than buying votes.
